title: Fitbit Sense ECG detection leading to diagnosis and treatment of ventricular tachycardia
summary: Fitbit Sense recorded an abnormal rhythm before clinicians diagnosed and treated ventricular tachycardia in India in October 2021.
account: A case report published in Cureus on 18 July 2023 describes a presentation in October 2021, without an exact day. A 55-year-old man in Jamshedpur, India, had symptoms at work. His Fitbit Sense watch detected an irregular heart rate of 164 beats per minute with irregular rhythm and bizarre QRS morphology. He sought care at Tata Main Hospital. A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) showed tachycardia at 166 beats per minute with bizarre QRS complexes under 130 ms and right axis deviation. Idiopathic fascicular ventricular tachycardia (VT) was diagnosed. After adenosine did not reverse the tachycardia, clinicians restored sinus rhythm through electrical cardioversion. They also corrected severe hypokalemia with intravenous potassium. Holter monitoring, echocardiography and coronary angiography excluded structural heart disease. He subsequently received oral verapamil and telmisartan. After four cardiology visits he was reported to be doing well with no further complaints.
purpose: The Fitbit Sense ECG app records a single-lead ECG to assess heart rhythm (its clearance is for atrial fibrillation). Capturing an abnormal rhythm for medical review was its purpose, although VT is outside its validated classification.
system: Fitbit Sense ECG app and heart-rate monitoring

ratings.reason: One man received a confirmed diagnosis of fascicular ventricular tachycardia and effective medical control. A material benefit to one person.

ai_role.statement: The watch's rhythm analysis flagged an irregular 164 bpm rhythm with abnormal QRS morphology, which sent the patient to hospital. The diagnosis and treatment were made by cardiologists from a 12-lead ECG and further tests.

fields.account: A case report published in Cureus on 18 July 2023 describes a presentation in October 2021, without an exact day. A 55-year-old man in Jamshedpur, India, had symptoms at work. His Fitbit Sense watch detected an irregular heart rate of 164 beats per minute with irregular rhythm and bizarre QRS morphology. He sought care at Tata Main Hospital. A 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) showed tachycardia at 166 beats per minute with bizarre QRS complexes under 130 ms and right axis deviation. Idiopathic fascicular ventricular tachycardia (VT) was diagnosed. After adenosine did not reverse the tachycardia, clinicians restored sinus rhythm through electrical cardioversion. They also corrected severe hypokalemia with intravenous potassium. Holter monitoring, echocardiography and coronary angiography excluded structural heart disease. He subsequently received oral verapamil and telmisartan. After four cardiology visits he was reported to be doing well with no further complaints.
